recipes.name: Grilled Stuffed Portobello Mushrooms
ingredients_raw: 0.5 cup finely chopped red bell pepper

steps.text: Preheat an outdoor grill for medium, indirect heat and lightly oil the grate.
Combine bell pepper, oil, garlic, salt, black pepper, and onion powder in a large bowl; spread over gill sides of mushroom caps.
Place mushrooms, stuffed sides up, over indirect heat, cover, and grill for 15 to 20 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Grilled Stuffed Portobello Mushrooms
raw_recipe.description: These grilled stuffed portobello mushrooms feature red bell pepper, fresh garlic, and onion powder. Grilled to perfection, they’re meaty and flavorful.

review.reviewBody: Excellent recipe! Instead of grilling the mushrooms, I laid foil on a baking sheet, arranged the mushrooms on there, and then spooned the mixture over them. I then baked in the oven at 350 degrees for about 7 minutes and broiled for another 5. Very tasty!!!

A keeper! I grilled the mushroom caps gills down for about 5 minutes and then flipped them and added the pepper filling. I also added a splash of balsamic vinegar to each cap (after I had filled them with the pepper mixture).

I had 2 large port. mushrooms to use up and tried this recipe. I chopped up 1 large red bell pepper along with 1/4 cup ch. sweet onion, 1 tsp. minced garlic and sauteed in a very small amount of olive oil till tender. Added the onion powder, some garlic powder and blk. pepper. No salt. Also added about 2 tbls. of white balsamic vincegar (from T. Joes). let sit while I grilled the mushrooms a few minutes on each side (sprayed both sides with Garlic Olive Oil)I let them drain well on paper towels before filling. Put them in a foil baking pan directly on a low heat grill and heated till hot. Before heating sprinkled each with shredded Asaigo/Parm. cheese. Excellent!

Grill stem side down on alum foil 5 mins., turn & top with sautéed onion & red pepper in olive oil, Italian seasoning. WOW it up with drizzled balsamic dressing. Shredded provolone, feta or mozza plus a little grated Parmesan. Bake about 20 mins. @ 350. Serve with steak sauce.

Great recipe that everyone raved about, including the vegan. Followed directions with the exception that replaced the onion powder with 1/2 cup diced onion that I sautéed along with a couple cloves of garlic before mixing with red pepper etc. Following advice of another, grilled gill side down for 4 minutes, then filled and grilled @15 minutes. I won't bother with that extra step next time and will shorten total grill time to about 10 minutes (grilled chicken at same time, so fire may have been hotter). Definitely plan to make again, great as a side or the entrée.

Very tasty meal! And very forgiving. I added the mushroom stems, and cooked them with onions, garlic, jalapeno pepper in some olive oil. Also added basil, tomato, parmesan cheese to mixture. I put mixture on mushroom, added a splash of Balsamic vinegar. We cooked them on the grill and added provolone cheese at the end and cooked until melted. Absolutely delicious, Michael. Thank you for sharing!

These were fantastic! I used a whole pepper, added some red onion and sautéed the filling earlier in the day. Then I added breadcrumbs and balsamic vinegar to the filling as it didn't look like I was going to have enough filling for the caps. Topped it off with Parmesan cheese before grilling. Everyone raved about these babies. Don't forget to scrape out the gills before filling!

I read a review and baked it at 350 for 7 minutes and then broiled for 5 minutes. It came out Uhhhhmazing! I also cut back to half of the olive oil and half of the salt, and ever the garlic lover, I doubled that up :) delicious!!!

This was the first time portobello mushrooms turned out great for me. I followed the recipe while using some recommendations from the others. I added a splash of balsamic and baked them in the oven at 350* for 20 min then added mozzarella and broiled for a few minutes. Thanks for sharing!

I grabbed some portobello mushrooms spur of the moment on my last grocery shopping expedition. I wanted to grill them, but didn't have a specific recipe in mind. Allrecipes to the rescue, as usual. I found this recipe and followed a couple of reviewers recommendations: 1) grilling the non-gill side of the mushrooms for five minutes before adding the mixture, and 2) adding some balsamic vinegar to the mixture for added flavor. Then, I added one idea of my own, a little basil from our deck herb garden. And what a great flavor explosion it was. Excellent, and highly recommended!

I thought this recipe was great! There is a bit too much pepper but other then that, it is very tasty and I would definitely make it again but with less pepper. I followed what others were saying and baked at 350 for 7 min then broiled for 5min. I also omitted the oil and instead used a good amount of cooking spray and some water. I took a photo but its too small for them to let me upload it. Looks colorful and nice.
No changes in the ingredients but too hot outside to grill. Baked them proper. Wow!! Amazing flavor! Definitely making this a regular dish. Thanx so much.
We modified the recipe with chopped tomatoes and added grated Parmesan

We liked this but didn't hold together on the grill. Tried another time with mozzarella and Italian breadcrumbs added and that worked better and it absorbed the yummy juices. So easy to prep and makes a great addition to any grill meal!
It was the best I tasted I love mushrooms any kind edible.
I have to say I am SHOCKED at how good these mushrooms were. I bought two portobello mushrooms at the store to try it. This week I will buy six. They are sooo good!!!!!

Allrecipes Magazine included this in it's Spring 2023 issue, but with a few changes. The magazine version used significantly more red pepper and added fresh thyme to the mixture. I used their version and it was a hit. But my husband still wondered if an addition of heat (crushed red pepper?) or something would improve upon it. Next time I might try the magazine's suggestion of adding capers or anchovies.
Had a few portobellos that needed used, these were so delicious and very quick and easy to make. Will be making them again. I did grate some Parmesan on at the very end.
I’d Put a little less salt in it but very juicy and tasty!
